findings.evidence: 'n target values checked' is reported with different values. Abstract: 789 values | Results p.4: 879 values. Agreeing reports: 3 location(s) [Abstract, Results p.4, Sample p.3] vs 1 [Results p.4].

The Abstract gives 34 ('...hor involvement for 9 (36% [20,59]) articles; reproducible with author involvement for 6 (34% [8,47]) articles; not fully reproducibl...'); the body never states 34. The body sentence about the same quantity (shared words: articles, author, involvement, reproducible) gives 25: '...Prior to seeking original author involvement, all target values in 9 out of the 25 articles (36%, CI [19,57]) were reproducible, with the remaining 16 articles (64%, CI [43,81]) containing at least one major numerical discrepancy....'. Confirm that both refer to the same quantity (same cohort, test set, metric) before keeping it.

The same digits in a different order for values: 789 ('...Overall, 37 major numerical discrepancies remained out of 789 checked values (5% [3,6]), but original conclusions did not appear affected....') and 879 ('...After author involvement, 37 major numerical discrepancies remained among the 879 target values examined across all articles (5%, CI [3,6])....'). If both count the same set, one of them has transposed digits.

The text reports an additional study or analysis: 'A comparison sample of 30 articles from the same journal without open data badges, checked with the same protocol, contained at least one major numerical discrepancy in 21 (70%) articles.'. Its head count 30 appears nowhere else in the paper, the phrase 'comparison sample' is used in no other sentence (the Methods do not describe it), the sentence cites no source, and the code, README and file names in the materials do not contain the number. Look for its data, code, table or supplementary item; if there is none, the analysis cannot be checked from what was released.
